items.headline: Polish Cabinet approves aid for farmers hit by weather
items.shortSummary: The Council of Ministers adopted a regulation expanding financial aid for farmers affected by weather events in 2026. Support includes payments for crop losses and loans for farmers.
items.summary: The Council of Ministers adopted a regulation changing the rules for the Agency for Restructuring and Modernization of Agriculture. The decision expands financial aid for farmers who suffered losses due to adverse weather. Aid will cover crops damaged by spring frosts, hail, heavy rain, or hurricanes. The damage must be estimated by a commission and exceed 30% of the average annual plant production. Support will also be available for fruit and vegetable producers whose crops suffered from temperatures of at least 37°C on 27–29 June 2026. The aid for purchasing a purebred bull will increase from 5,000 zlotys to 7,000 zlotys. New support options are introduced for pig breeders who bought breeding sows with verified origin. The rules for verifying the insurance condition for cultivated areas are changed. The condition will be met if at least 50% of the area was insured in the year of the damage. The rules for financing obligations related to the farm are clarified. New provisions detail the granting of loans to pay off due civil law obligations, such as debts from contracts. The "Report Agricultural Damage" application will be managed by the President of the Agency for Restructuring…

items.headline: Poland adopts Data Act implementation bill
items.shortSummary: Poland's cabinet adopted a bill to implement EU Data Act rules. It sets up a data ombudsman and dispute resolution rules for connected devices.
items.summary: The Council of Ministers adopted a bill to implement EU Data Act rules in Poland. The bill ensures the use of EU principles for data access and use. It covers data from internet-connected devices. The President of the Office of Electronic Communications will oversee compliance and handle complaints. The Minister of Digitalization will handle reporting to the European Commission. The Data Act facilitates data access for businesses, consumers, and the public administration. The bill clarifies obligations for institutions and helps users enforce their rights. Users will be able to access data from smart home devices and cars. They can also share this data with service providers. The bill establishes a data ombudsman role for the communications regulator. This official will monitor the market and cooperate with national and EU bodies. Users can file complaints about access disputes, contract restrictions, or refusals to share data. Dispute resolution entities must be certified. The regulator will check their independence and expertise. Certificates are valid for 5 years with possible extensions. The new rules will enter into force 3 months after publication in the Journal of Laws.

items.summary: The Czech government approved a new statute for the Council of Government for National Minorities on 21 September 2026. items.headline: Govt approves 45m euros for Ceuta financial stability
items.shortSummary: The Council of Ministers approved a decree law granting 45 million euros to Ceuta to cover migration crisis costs and maintain essential services. The decree also exempts the city from budget rules.
items.summary: The Council of Ministers approved a decree law with urgent measures to support the city of Ceuta. The law grants a direct subsidy of over 45 million euros, split into 40.6 million for current expenses and 4.6 million for capital expenses. These funds will cover essential services like health, education, and security. The decree also exempts Ceuta from submitting an economic-financial plan in 2026 or 2027 if it cannot meet stability targets due to these extra costs. Additionally, the government approved the II Plan de Acción de Juventud, a strategy for youth policy until 2028 with an investment of nearly 60,000 million euros. The government also approved a decree modifying the regulation on free legal aid to strengthen the right to effective judicial protection.
items.originalTitle: El Gobierno destina 45 millones de euros a garantizar la estabilidad financiera de Ceuta

top.shortSummary: The Chamber of Deputies proposed a bill to restrict government benefits during election years. It requires financial proof before creating new benefits.
top.summary: The Chamber of Deputies presented bill PLP 270/2026. The bill changes the Fiscal Responsibility Law and the Electoral Law. It sets limits on creating, instituting, expanding, or granting government benefits during election years. It also requires a prior demonstration of budget and financial adequacy. The goal is to strengthen the prevention of using public machinery for electoral purposes.
